cat.name: CAT
tips: Sections are timed and locked: you cannot go back, so spend the 40 minutes on the questions you can win.
Typed answers have no negative marking: always attempt them.
cat.gradable_note: VARC here has only vocabulary/grammar items (real VARC is mostly reading comprehension, which needs passages) and DILR has no questions yet (it needs data sets). Those sections are skipped or short until content is added.

conflicts: Question count: 66 (24 VARC / 20 DILR / 22 QA) in 2021-2024; CAT 2025 analysis reports 68 (24 / 22 / 22). Encoded as 68.
A CAT 2026 pattern was not found; the CAT 2025 pattern is used.
source.notes: 120 minutes, three 40-minute sections in fixed order (VARC, DILR, QA), no switching back. +3 per correct, -1 per wrong MCQ, no negative marking for typed answers.

sections.subject: Maths

tips: No negative marking: never leave an MCQ blank.
Show full steps in written sections; they carry method marks.
cbse10_maths.gradable_note: The real paper is 80 marks / 3 hours (Sections A-E: 20 MCQ x1, 5 VSA x2, 6 SA x3, 4 LA x5, 3 case studies x4). Only Sections A and B (30 marks) can be auto-graded here, so time is scaled to 68 min. Written and case-study sections need a teacher or rubric.

source.notes: Section structure 20/5/6/4/3 questions = 80 marks, 3 hours, no negative marking. Confirm against the current CBSE sample paper.

jee_main.name: JEE Main (Paper 1, B.E./B.Tech)
tips: Do the sure-shot MCQs first: every wrong MCQ costs 1 mark.
Numerical answers have no options to fall back on: check units and rounding.

conflicts: Negative marking for numerical-value questions: PW, Motion and Allen say -1 applies to both sections (Allen calls it a 2026 change); Careers360 says numerical questions have no negative marking. Encoded as -1.
Older patterns let you attempt 5 of 10 numerical questions per subject; 2026 sources say all 5 are compulsory. Encoded as compulsory.
source.notes: 75 questions (25 per subject = 20 MCQ + 5 numerical), +4 per correct. Duration 180 min is the long-standing value but was not shown in the retrieved pages. Check the NTA information bulletin before relying on any of this.

neet_ug.name: NEET UG
tips: Biology (Botany + Zoology) is half the paper: NCERT line-by-line is the highest-yield habit.
A wrong answer costs 1 mark; skip only when you can't narrow to two options.

conflicts: Duration: most sources say 3 hours; one lists 3 hours 15 minutes for a 're-NEET' sitting. Encoded as 180 min.
Wording of the penalty varies ('1/4 of marks' vs '-1'); both mean -1 for a 4-mark question.
source.notes: 180 MCQs (45 each in Physics, Chemistry, Botany, Zoology), +4/-1, 720 marks, Section B removed. Check the NTA bulletin.

upsc_csat.name: UPSC Prelims: CSAT (Paper II)
tips: CSAT is only qualifying, but scoring under 33% (66/200) ends the attempt whatever your GS score.
Many aspirants lose marks to negative marking by over-attempting.
upsc_csat.gradable_note: Real CSAT has ~25-30 reading-comprehension questions; none are included yet (they need passages). Only numeracy items are here.

source.notes: 80 questions x 2.5 marks, 2 hours, -1/3 per wrong answer, qualifying at 33%.

upsc_gs1.name: UPSC Prelims: General Studies Paper I
tips: One-third of a question's marks is deducted for each wrong answer: guess only after eliminating options.
Static portions repay revision; track current affairs separately.
upsc_gs1.gradable_note: All factual questions here are authored from standard textbook facts and marked UNREVIEWED: a subject expert must check them, and current-affairs items are deliberately not included.

source.notes: 100 questions x 2 marks, 2 hours, -1/3 per wrong answer. Counts toward the Prelims cut-off.
